subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: LH-FSH Ratio in PCOS

steps.tx: **Luteinizing hormone** hypersecretion accompanied by an altered LH to FSH ratio of 2:1 or 3:1 represents a classic neuroendocrine hallmark of polycystic ovary syndrome. Accelerated hypothalamic GnRH pulse frequency selectively stimulates transcription of the luteinizing hormone beta-subunit over the follicle-stimulating hormone beta-subunit. Although historically prized in diagnostic evaluations, international consensus guidelines no longer mandate an elevated LH to FSH ratio as an obligatory criterion because normal ratios occur in over forty percent of confirmed cases.
steps.say: An inverted LH to FSH ratio of two-to-one or three-to-one is a classic neuroendocrine feature of PCOS, driven by fast GnRH pulses. However, international guidelines no longer require it for diagnosis because many patients have normal ratios.

steps.tx: **Theca cell hyperplasia** develops in response to chronically elevated circulating luteinizing hormone levels acting on theca interna cells. LH stimulates the key steroidogenic regulatory enzyme CYP17A1 (possessing 17-alpha-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase activities), driving marked overproduction of androstenedione and testosterone. Hyperinsulinaemia acts synergistically with LH at the theca cell level, amplifying androgen synthesis. Excess androgens enter the circulation, provoking clinical hirsutism, cystic acne, and male-pattern androgenic alopecia.
steps.say: High LH directly stimulates ovarian theca cells, up-regulating the CYP17A1 enzyme to overproduce testosterone and androstenedione. Hyperinsulinaemia acts synergistically with LH, worsening hyperandrogenism.

nodes.label: High LH Pulses
nodes.sub: Accelerated GnRH stimulates theca LH receptors

nodes.label: Follicular Arrest
nodes.sub: Preantral follicles arrest at 2 to 9 mm stage

steps.tx: **Follicular arrest** occurs in polycystic ovary syndrome because relatively deficient follicle-stimulating hormone levels fail to cross the threshold required to induce granulosa cell aromatase (CYP19A1). The androgen-rich microenvironment within developing follicles suppresses normal granulosa cell proliferation. Follicles arrest development at the small antral stage, measuring two to nine millimetres in diameter, and fail to select a dominant pre-ovulatory follicle. These arrested follicles accumulate in the ovarian cortex, producing the characteristic necklace of pearls ultrasound appearance.
steps.say: Follicles arrest at the two to nine millimetre stage because relatively low FSH cannot stimulate granulosa aromatase to convert androgens into estrogen. No follicle becomes dominant, creating the string-of-pearls appearance.

points: Adequate cyclic FSH rises above threshold

right.title: PCOS Follicular Arrest
points: Relative FSH deficit below induction threshold
High local androgens suppress granulosa cells

steps.tx: **Anti-Mullerian hormone** (AMH) is produced exclusively by the granulosa cells of preantral and small antral follicles up to eight millimetres in diameter. In polycystic ovary syndrome, serum AMH concentrations are elevated two- to four-fold above age-matched reference ranges, directly reflecting the massive expansion of arrested small antral follicles. Circulating AMH acts as a physiological inhibitor of follicular maturation, suppressing FSH-induced aromatase expression and further reinforcing the cycle of anovulation.
steps.say: Serum anti-Mullerian hormone is elevated two- to four-fold in PCOS, produced by the massive pool of arrested small follicles. AMH actively inhibits FSH sensitivity, worsening ovulatory arrest.

vis.title: Endocrine Biomarkers in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
rows: Subthreshold levels fail to select dominant follicle
Reflects expanded pool of arrested antral follicles

steps.tx: **Sex hormone-binding globulin** (SHBG) synthesis by hepatocytes is powerfully suppressed by circulating hyperinsulinaemia. Even in patients whose total testosterone remains in the high-normal or borderline range, suppressed SHBG levels drastically increase the free, unbound, biologically active fraction of testosterone. Free androgen index (FAI), calculated as total testosterone divided by SHBG multiplied by one hundred, exceeding a cut-off of four to five serves as a sensitive biochemical indicator of hyperandrogenism.
steps.say: Hyperinsulinaemia suppresses liver production of sex hormone-binding globulin. This drives up free active testosterone, meaning patients can have severe hirsutism even when total testosterone is only borderline elevated.

nodes.sub: Reduced plasma binding capacity for androgens

nodes.label: Target Organ Binding
nodes.sub: Hair follicle 5-alpha reductase converts to DHT

steps.tx: **Early follicular phase** testing on menstrual cycle day two, three, or four is mandatory when obtaining basal gonadotropin and androgen levels. Testing during this quiescent phase avoids confounding physiological LH surges that occur during ovulation. If a patient is amenorrhoeic, blood testing can be performed randomly, provided serum progesterone is under five nanomoles per litre to exclude recent ovulation, alongside measurement of serum human chorionic gonadotropin to rule out unrecognized pregnancy.
steps.say: Draw blood for LH, FSH, and androgens on cycle days two through four. Testing during the early follicular phase avoids mid-cycle LH surges that distort the true baseline ratio.

vis.title: Diagnostic Blood Panel Protocol in Suspected PCOS
rows: Elevated FSH >25 IU/L indicates ovarian insufficiency
Values >6 nmol/L mandate CAH synacthen test

steps.tx: **Non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia** represents the most critical endocrine mimic that must be differentiated from an altered LH to FSH ratio. Caused by partial 21-hydroxylase deficiency, it presents with identical clinical features of hirsutism, oligomenorrhoea, and polycystic ovaries. Baseline morning follicular phase 17-hydroxyprogesterone (17-OHP) must be measured: values below 6 nanomoles per litre exclude the disease, while values exceeding 30 nanomoles per litre confirm it, with intermediate values requiring an ACTH stimulation test.
steps.say: Always exclude late-onset congenital adrenal hyperplasia by checking 17-hydroxyprogesterone. Partial 21-hydroxylase deficiency mimics PCOS perfectly but requires glucocorticoids rather than standard ovarian therapy.

left.title: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
points: Primary therapy with COCPs and lifestyle

steps.tx: **Combined oral contraceptives** containing anti-androgenic progestins provide the cornerstone pharmacotherapy for normalizing gonadotropin ratios and controlling hyperandrogenism in PCOS patients not seeking pregnancy. Exogenous ethinylestradiol suppresses hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility and pituitary LH secretion, depriving theca cells of stimulation and halting ovarian androgen production. Simultaneously, oral estrogen stimulates hepatic synthesis of sex hormone-binding globulin, clearing free bioavailable testosterone and resolving acne and hirsutism.
steps.say: Combined oral contraceptive pills are the mainstay of medical treatment. Estrogen shuts down excessive pituitary LH secretion, starving theca cells of androgen-stimulating signals, while doubling SHBG to soak up free testosterone.
